slides.title: Made for everyone
slides.text: People see, hear, read and move in different ways. A good game works for all of them.
slides.alt: Design Lab opens with a user to design for: their needs come first, before any setting is touched.

slides.title: Every switch is for someone
slides.text: Open a game's settings: captions, read-aloud, text size, contrast. Each switch was made for someone.
slides.alt: The audit round: a real game is checked setting by setting — captions, text size, contrast — for who each helps.

slides.title: Help one, help many
slides.text: Captions were made for people who can not hear. They also help anyone in a noisy room. A change for one person usually helps many.
slides.alt: A second Design Lab user: a change made for one person usually turns out to help many more.

slides.title: Who does it help?
slides.text: Match each change to the people it helps. Most changes help more than one group.

big text: hard to see, bright sun

slides.title: Ask for ideas
slides.text: Ask someone else what they would change. Other people's ideas, called perspectives, spot things you did not think of.
slides.alt: The audit round: a real game is checked setting by setting — captions, text size, contrast — for who each helps.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Inside the Machine at Design Lab. Fill in the audit with 4 settings, then solve all three briefs. Watch where the user struggles.
